theory.intro: Data can be shown using different displays. Stem-and-leaf plots and frequency histograms require numerical data, whereas column graphs can display categorical or numerical data. Each display has a set way of placing the data onto the picture.
steps: Choose the stems from the place value of the data.
Write each leaf next to its stem.
Order the leaves in each row from smallest to largest.
Add a key that shows how to read a stem and a leaf.

workedExamples.question_text:
The numbers of books borrowed by 10 students are $0,1,2,1,3,2,1,5,2,0$.
(a) Construct a frequency table and a dot plot.
(b) How many students borrowed exactly 1 book?
(c) How many borrowed more than 2 books?
(d) What percentage borrowed at least 3 books?
Construct an ordered stem-and-leaf plot for $42,18,24,54,22,18,47,21,56$. Use all digits except the last as the stem and give a key.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use stems 1 to 5. Write each final digit beside its stem, then order the leaves from smallest to largest. Keep stem 3 with no leaves because there are no values in the 30s.

$\begin{array}{c|l}\text{Stem}&\text{Leaf}\\\hline1&8\;8\\2&1\;2\;4\\3&\\4&2\;7\\5&4\;6\end{array}$

Key: $2\mid4$ means 24. Each leaf represents one data value.

workedExamples.question_text:
The stem-and-leaf plot shows scores.

$\begin{array}{c|l}\text{Stem}&\text{Leaf}\\\hline2&3\;8\\3&1\;5\;5\\4&0\;6\\5&1\end{array}$

Key: $2\mid3$ means 23.
What is the highest score?
workedExamples.solution_text: Read the largest stem and its largest leaf. The final row has stem 5 and leaf 1, so the highest score is 51.

(a) The salad column reaches halfway between 6 and 8, so 7 salad sandwiches were sold.

(b) Read both column heights: chicken is 9 and cheese is 4. Subtract to compare them.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}9-4\\&=5\text{ sandwiches}\end{aligned}$

(a) Read the height of the column centred on score 4. Its frequency is 5.

(b) The tallest columns are centred on scores 3 and 5. Both have frequency 7, so both scores are most frequent.

foundation.question_text:
A die is rolled $10$ times: $1, 4, 2, 4, 6, 3, 4, 2, 5, 1$.
Display this data as a dot plot.

The colours of $10$ counters are recorded: R, B, R, R, G, B, R, G, R, B.
In a frequency table of this data, what frequency is written for Red (R)?

Construct a stem-and-leaf plot for this data, using the tens digit as the stem. Give a key.
$22, 25, 25, 32, 36, 43$
foundation.solution_text:
Use stems $2, 3, 4$ and write the final digit of each value as its leaf, in order.
$\begin{array}{c|l}\text{Stem}&\text{Leaf}\\ \hline 2&2\;5\;5\\ 3&2\;6\\ 4&3\end{array}$
Key: $2\;|\;2$ means $22$.

Read the height of the Veggie column
$=6\text{ slices}$

Read the height of the column centred on size $7$
$=8$

Construct a stem-and-leaf plot for this data, using the tens digit as the stem:
$7, 12, 15, 15, 23, 24, 31$
development.solution_text:
1. **Choose the stems from the place value of the data.**
Stems are $0, 1, 2, 3$
2. **Write each leaf next to its stem.**
$\begin{array}{c|l}\text{Stem}&\text{Leaf}\\ \hline 0&7\\ 1&2\;5\;5\\ 2&3\;4\\ 3&1\end{array}$
Key: $1\;|\;2$ means $12$

The tallest column matches the largest frequency, $7$
Scores $11$ and $12$ both have frequency $7$
Tallest columns: $11$ and $12$

mastery.question_text:
Construct a stem-and-leaf plot for this data, using the tens digit as the stem:
$19, 22, 22, 26, 28, 40, 53, 55, 56$

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.85]\draw[{Stealth}-{Stealth}] (-0.6,0)--(5.6,0);\foreach \x in {0,1,2,3,4,5} {\draw (\x,0)--(\x,-0.12); \node[below] at (\x,-0.14) {$\x$};}\fill (0,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (0,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,0.94) circle (2.2pt);\fill (1,1.26) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (2,0.94) circle (2.2pt);\fill (3,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\fill (3,0.62) circle (2.2pt);\fill (5,0.3) circle (2.2pt);\node[below] at (2.5,-0.62) {Books borrowed in a week};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The dot plot shows the number of books $12$ students borrowed in a week.
What percentage of the students borrowed at least $3$ books?
mastery.solution_text:
At least $3$ books: $3$ books ($2$ students) and $5$ books ($1$ student)
$2+1=3\text{ students}$
$\frac{3}{12}\times100\%=25\%$
